_comment: Hand-labelled (requirement, bullet) pairs for fitting the semantic-coverage threshold (issue #126). Built only from the synthetic benchmark profiles in eval/profiles/ (never personal/): every `text` is verbatim from the named profile, except the `aspiration` pairs and two `soft_skill` ones, whose bullets are synthetic (`origin: synthetic`) because no profile states an intention, or names a deadline or a process, in a bullet; an `education` pair's text is `education_text` of a profile's education entry (degree and institution, with dates only for a degree in progress); each aspiration bullet is about the tool its requirement names. The requirements are synthetic, written in job-posting style. `label` is the user-confirmed label (reviewed 2026-09-30 from REVIEW.md; every proposal kept as is except `ss_ownership_run`, relabelled not_covered: maintaining pipelines is not a stated instance of taking ownership): covered | not_covered. `literal` pairs share the requirement's own words with the bullet (the control the literal target already catches); `semantic` pairs meet the requirement in none of its words; `partial` pairs name the tool or area but the requirement asks for more (years, leadership, scale, production); `aspiration` pairs state interest or a plan; `near_miss` pairs are a related technology or domain; `unrelated` pairs are a different field; `boundary` pairs are contestable either way; `soft_skill` pairs are soft-skill requirements (deadlines, processes, communication, collaboration, ownership, attention to detail) against bullets that are real evidence (covered) or merely adjacent (not_covered), two of them the benchmark cases at 0.58 and 0.67; `education` pairs (`kind: education`) put an education entry, as text, against degree and enrollment requirements, including a wrong field, a wrong level and an in-progress degree. Regenerate the report with `python eval/fit_coverage_threshold.py analyze`.
